title: Can Language Models Reason about Individualistic Human Values and Preferences?
findings: Language models' accuracy in predicting individuals' religious values improves substantially when provided with examples (demonstrations) of their other values, increasing from as low as 37% to over 72% for models like GPT-4o. Compared to other demographic dimensions like continent or country of birth, the models exhibited lower performance variance (inequity) across different religious groups, suggesting a more consistent reasoning capability for values related to religion. Training a specialized model (INDIEVALUEREASONER) further improved performance and equity, with significant gains observed across all measured religious affiliations.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures a language model's ability to predict an individual's responses to questions about their religious values and practices (e.g., frequency of attending religious services) based on a set of their other, non-religious value-expressing statements. This is part of a broader task of reasoning about individualistic human values.
